quickAnswer: Yes—the UNESCO-listed Divriği Great Mosque and Hospital reopened on May 6, 2024, after a nine-year restoration and welcomes visitors daily in 2026 with free entry. Built in 1228–1229 under the Mengücek dynasty, its four deeply carved stone portals have no parallel in Islamic architecture. Reach Divriği via Sivas Airport (200 km) or TCDD's daily Sivas–Divriği regional train.

body.text: Is Divriği Great Mosque open after its multi-year restoration?

Yes. Following an extensive nine-year restoration from 2015 to 2024 led by the General Directorate of Foundations, the Great Mosque and adjoining Darüşşifa (Hospital) reopened for worship and visitors on May 6, 2024 ([Türkiye Today Reopening Report](https://www.turkiyetoday.com/culture/divrigi-great-mosque-darussifa-to-reopen-following-restoration-2792); [Turkish Airlines Divriği Guide](https://blog.turkishairlines.com/en/divrigi-travel-guide/)). Entry is free, and the complex welcomed around 400,000 visitors in the first nine months of 2026 ([Daily Sabah 2026 Report](https://www.dailysabah.com/arts/turkiyes-798-year-old-divrigi-great-mosque-draws-record-crowds/news)).

Restoration crews replaced the protective roof, laser-cleaned centuries of soot from the sculpted limestone, stabilized structural cracks, and cleared encroaching modern structures around the hillside perimeter. Because the mosque remains an active place of worship, dress modestly (headscarves for women and covered shoulders/knees for all visitors) and avoid touring the prayer hall during the five daily congregational prayer windows.
Why are its 13th-century carved stone portals considered unique in Islamic architecture?

Commissioned in 1228–1229 by Mengücek ruler Ahmet Shah and his wife Turan Melek—and built by master architect Hürremshah of Ahlat—the complex was among Türkiye's first sites inscribed on the [UNESCO World Heritage List](https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/tr/) in 1985. Its four monumental portals break from symmetrical Seljuk conventions, using deeply undercut, three-dimensional stone relief where thousands of botanical and geometric motifs never repeat identically ([UNESCO Divriği Gallery](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/358/gallery/); [Illustrarch Architectural Analysis](https://illustrarch.com/history-heritage/74243-divrigi-great-mosque.html)).
Each doorway carries its own sculptural grammar:

items: North Portal (Cennet / Paradise Gate): High-relief stone foliage, palmettes, and oversized medallions projecting outward almost like freestanding sculpture.

West Portal (Çarşı / Textile Gate): Finer geometric lacework echoing medieval woven fabrics; between May and September, late-afternoon sunlight casts a silhouette resembling a praying figure across the stone.
East Portal (Şah / Royal Gate): Cleaner Seljuk geometric framing leading toward the elevated royal gallery.
Darüşşifa (Hospital) Portal: Monumental pointed arch opening into a two-story vaulted healing hall centered on an octagonal pool once used for water-sound therapy.

body.text: How do you reach Divriği via Sivas Airport or regional train?

Fly into [Sivas Nuri Demirağ Airport (VAS)](https://dhmi.gov.tr/sayfalar/havalimani/sivas/anasayfa.aspx), located 22 km northwest of Sivas city center and roughly 200 km (2.5 to 3 hours by car) from Divriği. Travelers preferring rail can ride the twice-daily TCDD regional train linking Sivas, Divriği, and Erzincan, booking seats online via [TCDD Taşımacılık E-Bilet](https://ebilet.tcddtasimacilik.gov.tr/).

You can also reach Sivas from Ankara in roughly 2.5 hours on Türkiye's High-Speed Train (YHT), stay overnight in Sivas city, and catch the morning regional train to Divriği—a scenic 2.5-to-3-hour journey through Anatolian river canyons—before returning to Sivas in the late afternoon.

body.text: What else is worth seeing in Sivas city?

Spend at least one full day in central Sivas around the Historic City Square (Kent Meydanı), where three 13th-century Seljuk madrasas stand within five minutes' walk of one another alongside the Atatürk and Congress Museum ([GoTürkiye 48 Hours in Sivas](https://goturkiye.com/sivas/48-hours)). Pair the monuments with a coffee break inside 19th-century Taşhan and a lunch of Sivas köfte or flaky Sivas katmeri.
Highlights within Sivas's walkable center include:

items: Çifte Minareli Medrese (1271): Towering twin brick-and-tile minarets framing a richly carved Seljuk stone facade.
Şifaiye Medrese (1217): Directly opposite Çifte Minareli, housing the tiled tomb of Seljuk Sultan İzzeddin Keykavus I.
Buruciye Medrese (1271) & Gök Medrese (1271): Finely proportioned courtyards showcasing turquoise tilework and carved stone inscriptions.

Sivas Atatürk and Congress Museum: The 1892 school building where Mustafa Kemal Atatürk chaired the September 4–11, 1919 Sivas Congress ([Turkish Museums: Sivas City Guide](https://turkishmuseums.com/blog/detail/city-guide-sivas/10097/4)).
Visit between May and October for clear mountain roads and late-afternoon light on the West Portal; winters bring heavy snow.
Plan to arrive at Divriği Great Mosque by late morning, then return to the West Portal in mid-to-late afternoon (May–September) to observe the changing relief shadows.
Walk up to Divriği Castle and the restored Ottoman adobe mansions (such as Şeyhoğlu Mansion) while in town.
Pre-book TCDD regional train tickets on weekends and national holidays, as seats sell out early.
Carry modest mosque attire and slip-on shoes for entering the prayer hall.

faq.q: Is there an entrance fee for Divriği Great Mosque and Hospital?
faq.a: No. Both the Great Mosque and the adjoining Darüşşifa (Hospital) are free to enter daily, though visitors should check local prayer times before stepping inside the main mosque hall.

faq.q: Can you visit Divriği as a day trip from Sivas?
faq.a: Yes. Driving from central Sivas takes roughly 2 hours each way (about 175 km), and the morning TCDD regional train also allows a full-day visit with an afternoon return train.

faq.q: What time does the "praying man" shadow appear on the West Portal?
faq.a: Between May and September, the late-afternoon sun (typically around ikindi / mid-to-late afternoon) casts a human-like silhouette across the carved stone of the West Portal.

faq.q: Are there good hotels in Divriği town?
faq.a: Divriği has a small number of modest guesthouses and restored boutique mansions, but wider hotel selection and dining options are found in Sivas city center.

faq.q: How does the Eastern Express (Doğu Ekspresi) connect to Divriği?
faq.a: The main Eastern Express and Touristic Eastern Express pass through Divriği station on the Ankara–Kars corridor, though the Sivas–Divriği–Erzincan regional train is far easier to book for a targeted Sivas–Divriği round trip.

faq.q: How much time do you need at the Great Mosque and Hospital?
faq.a: Allow at least 90 minutes to 2 hours to study all four exterior portals, the vaulted prayer hall, the wooden 1240 minbar, and the hospital interior without rushing.
